description: Orca is the ADE for working with a fleet of parallel agents. Run any coding agent with your own subscription. Available on desktop, mobile and remote runtime.
vibe: Ship cross-platform, cross-version, cross-host code that never lies about what it knows.
highlights: Design system is linted, not suggested: raw palette colors, restyled primitives, and computed className strings fail CI.
Never steal monitor focus in tests — no show(), bringToFront(), or app.focus(); use CDP screenshots of hidden renderers.
Vague module names (helpers, utils, common, misc) are banned; files must be named after the concrete domain concept they contain.
Remote verdict vocabulary is fixed: live / unverifiable / exited, with no synonyms, because loss of contact is never evidence of process death.
Git 2.25 is the compatibility floor; every new subcommand needs a version boundary, a fallback, and a capability cache scoped to the executing host.
assessment: This file encodes hard-won operational scars rather than aspirational style: Windows EDR scoring, MSYS path rewriting, glibc floors, and mixed-version wire compatibility are all treated as first-class constraints. The result is an unusually honest architecture doc where every rule traces back to a real failure mode, and enforcement is pushed into lint gates instead of reviewer memory. It is the rare AGENTS.md that would actually prevent a production incident.
